newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crudes rise with WTI, players absent.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crudes rise with WTI, players absent.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices rose with West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude, but trade remained dead with players attending an industry function or waiting for Canadian pricing next week.
Alaska North Slope (ANS) buyers continued to turn away offers, with outright prices too costly at a time when local margins are down 21 percent from last quarter.
"It's just too expensive and the margin's not there," one West Coast trader said.
Weak margins might force Ultramar to cut runs at its Wilmington, Calif., plant from late October through November.
Ultramar said it declined to buy an ANS cargo for November, which would trim crude imput 12,000 barrels-per-day.
Tosco Corp was also considering run cuts at its California refineries, traders said.
Outright ANS prices rose 15 cents to $22.80/23.10 a barrel, in line with a 20 cent rise in WTI.

Bellwether WTI gained on supportive data from Thursday's Energy Information Administration (EIA) report, which showed crude inventories fell 3.3 million barrels last week compared to the API's 417,000 barrels.
One West Coast trader speculated the planned outage at Chevron's El Segundo plant would trim West Coast gasoline inventories next week.
Traders said Chevron was offering its backed-up crude, but could not specify what grades.
Bids remained notionally $2.50 under November WTI, but a major producer said his $2.10 offer might tighten because its value was relatively cheap compared to imports.
But one buyer disagreed, claiming Oriente crude was talked cheaper than ANS.
Line 63 diffs remained unchanged at $3.20 to $3.00 under spot WTI for November delivery.
ARCO will announce November shipping restrictions for the line next week, traders said.
California heavy crudes remained flat. Kern River crude was $17.30/17.50 a barrel.
Values for Wilmington crude stayed $18.65/18.75 a barrel.
